candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a mixed number or whole number as an equivalent improper fraction (or as a fraction with a specified denominator) to enable fraction operations.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three describe converting mixed/whole numbers into improper fractions or equivalent fractions with a specified denominator; B names it more broadly but matches the same conversion operation.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) for unlike fractions to prepare for subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A separates 'choose common denominator' from scaling, while B and C bundle choosing (often via LCM) with rewriting; this concept captures the denominator-selection/LCM portion.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite one or more fractions as equivalent fractions by multiplying numerator and denominator to reach a chosen common denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A explicitly isolates scaling to equivalent fractions; B and C include scaling inside their 'find common denominator' skill, so their same skill_id maps one-to-many to both C02 (choose/LCM) and C03 (scaling).

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference once quantities are in compatible form by subtracting numerators over a common denominator and/or subtracting whole and fractional parts and recombining.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three include the actual subtraction step after alignment; A’s version also mentions simplification, but the core shared concept is performing the subtraction once denominators/forms are compatible.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the resulting fraction to lowest terms and express the final value in an acceptable form such as an integer, irreducible fraction, or mixed number.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B and C explicitly separate simplification/final formatting; A includes these actions inside its subtraction skill, so A:S04 maps to both subtraction (C04) and simplification/formatting (C05).

alignment_summary: Across the three codebooks, the shared workflow is: convert mixed/whole numbers as needed, establish a common denominator, scale to equivalent fractions, perform subtraction, then simplify/format. Key granularity differences: A splits common-denominator selection vs scaling, while B and C combine them; A also bundles simplification into its subtraction skill, requiring one-to-many mappings for A:S04 and for B:S01/C:S02.
